patches.title: reserved words as exported names
patches.origin: local; found by npm top-100 sweep

evidence.spec: ExportSpecifier's exported name is a ModuleExportName, i.e. an IdentifierName, so reserved words are legal after `as`. The local name before `as` is left reserved on purpose: without a from-clause an early error requires an IdentifierReference, so `export { import }` must keep failing (test/negative/export-reserved-local-name.mjs).

first_seen.note: lib/index.js — `export { _import as import }` in the generated re-export list; 1 file

patches.title: automatic semicolon before a subscript or call that cannot continue an expression
patches.origin: local; found by npm top-100 sweep

evidence.spec: The scanner refused ASI before `[` and `(` unconditionally, because they usually continue an expression (`a\n[0]` is `a[0]`). It now refuses only where an expression can actually be continued, which it already knows from valid_symbols[LOGICAL_OR] — the same signal it uses for comments. After a bare declarator, `return`, or a class field name no binary operator may follow either, and there the spec inserts the semicolon.

first_seen.note: lib/argparse.js:1874 — `let subnamespace` then a destructuring assignment on the next line; 1 file

evidence.also_fixes: two silent misparses upstream produced without erroring: `return\n[1]` parsed as returning the array rather than as a bare return, and `class C { x\n[y] = 1 }` parsed the field name as a subscript
